lastCompletedStory.title: Add an empty-push (ahead_by>=1) gate on the worker pass path

nextStoryContext: US-004 added a branch-level empty-push gate: readWorkerOutcome (src/supervisor/result.ts) now accepts an optional `aheadByForBranch?: () => number | null` option, consulted (confirmEmptyPushGate) right after confirmCommitGate passes in BOTH DONE branches (worker-report-primary and handoff-fallback). ahead_by===0 resolves to kind:'blocked' (NOT a new WorkerOutcomeKind -- deliberately reuses 'blocked' so loop.ts's existing outcome.kind==='blocked'->blockedResult terminal path handles it identically to a failed ensurePushed push-verification check, per the AC's own phrasing). requires:'operator' stories are exempt (isOperatorStory reused verbatim from confirmCommitGate). A null return (git rev-list could not be evaluated) is fail-open (ok:true), asymmetric with commitExistsForStory's fail-closed catch block -- this gate is a coarse belt-and-suspenders check layered on top of push-verification, not a replacement, so a git hiccup should never spuriously block a real pass. host.ts's aheadByForBranch adapter (git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD, best-effort git fetch origin main first, falling back to local main..HEAD) is a direct sibling of commitExistsForStory's fetch+range-fallback logic immediately above it in the same file. loop.ts threads the new RunSupervisorOptions.aheadByForBranch field straight into every readWorkerOutcome call, same pattern as commitExistsForStory. Loop-level integration test gotcha: a gate that only fires on the DONE-outcome-resolution path needs the two-prd-snapshot array pattern (passes:false at the top of the iteration so decideNextAction dispatches 'implement', passes:true by outcome-resolution time) -- a single static passes:true snapshot never reaches worker-dispatch at all (decideNextAction picks review/complete instead) and the loop silently spins to max-iterations instead of blocking on iteration 1 (caught and fixed during this story; see patterns.md). No production caller currently sets a real ahead-by ceiling threshold beyond >=1 (i.e. no multi-commit-squash-detection use case yet); if a future story wants richer push-shape validation (e.g. detecting an oversized or unexpectedly-multi-commit push), it can build on aheadByForBranch's return value without touching the gate's exemption/fail-open semantics.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed --count prints the commit count for the given range, and A..B range syntax (shorthand for ^A B) lists commits reachable from B but not A; a range with nothing ahead outputs 0 with --count. Matches the aheadByForBranch implementation (Number("0") === 0 triggers the gate).
